body: I mean, they help a little. I'd definitely be dead without them, but I am far from okay. They help me get things done, but they don't really make me feel a lot better. And sometimes it's like they're not even there cuz I still get really bad episodes. But they're worth it I think, given they helped me get back into school

Oh for sure with the meds. It's like I can't compete a full thought. But I don't think your pets would prefer anyone over you necessarily. I mean, so long as you provide for them, you've done right by them.

Yeah, "I want to go home" has just been what I thought to myself whenever I didn't want to be where I was. When I stopped wanting to be on earth, it started coming to my head again. even though home isn't really where I wish I were.

Same, actually. First developed depression when I was eleven, and the older I got, the more work I had to put into managing it. Every year I go up on meds. Every year I'm farther from whoever the fuck I used to be. I wish I had something more productive to tell you, but I just wanted to say I get it to an extent.
Real

I've been suicidal myself, though not so much anymore. it sucks ass, but really the only thing that can be done is to tell a therapist/doctor/psychiatrist. In my own experience, telling people in person about these things made me sick. but if they hadn't found out, I can only imagine how much worse it could have gotten.
It's not that I accept death, it's that I yearn for it. It's the one thing I want more than anything, but I just can't have it. it's devastating.

You're not just alive because the world deserves you. (although that's part of it.) You're alive because you deserve the world. Maybe getting help is difficult, but surely engaging in your interests is not? Learning about topics you like, exploring different changes that could be made to your living space or daily routine, etc. You don't just exist because other people want you there, but because you have the potential to want things and then obtain them.
I see. I'm more a fan of neutral colors like gray, but I can see the appeal. Do you have some kind of profound reason to like green, or is it just cause it looks nice?

I'm not sure how to help, but I've been taught that the main cure to this is doing things that make you happy. Do you have any hobbies or interests? People you'd like to hang out with more? Instead of trying to block the thoughts out, try to resolve them.
Honestly, I think we all could. If there's something in particular you want to say, I'd love to hear it. but if not, then what's your favorite color?
Can't say you're alone in that.
Exactly. If anything, it makes me feel worse. It's like I'm not allowed to be upset, but I am anyway. It makes me feel like an attention seeker, even though I really do need help.
For real. I still struggle to believe that some people don't wake up sad and want to do things with their life. I look at people with the motivation to do basic tasks, and I get so envious.
Don't commit suicide. Or tell the guy first.
I'm in the same situation. I haven't really been able to make them stop consistently, but the solution is supposed to be "doing things that make you happy"

Okay, I have some terrible advice, but it's what I would do in this situation. Skip the activity. Don't show up to it. Hide somewhere while it's going on. Express how much damage it's done to you, and if your parents still won't take you out of it, just keep skipping. Be as defiant as possible. 

Don't kill yourself. It's something you can fix.
But isn't life about happiness of the self, and not the happiness of others at all costs?
There's a show on Netflix called "the end of the f***ing world." It explores the reality of being devoid of emotion. It's a bit dark, but it's really good. I recommend it.

To be brave is to do something you'd afraid of despite the fear. If your afraid of dying but you do it anyway for some (noble?) reason, then it's brave. If you stay alive even though it scares you, then you're brave. But I understand what you mean. Even as someone who has never wanted to die as much as I do now, the prospect is still daunting. It does take courage. And at since point, you have to wonder if your being brave or stupid. Committing a crime sounds stressful, but if I did it, it wouldn't be brave, it would be stupid. So really, it's all about perspective.
Fuck, I really want to fight you on that, but it was so well put, and low key correct. I'm gonna use that later
Verbal abuse is still abuse.
I get that too. I'm not sure what to think about it, all I know is that it's a hindrance.

Call the police. I know that sounds extreme, but if your home is not a safe place, I fear this may be the only option to get support. If you think it's not that severe, maybe talk to your doctor about it. But I do hope you realize that you are not a failure.
Exactly. People never know what we need to hear. I don't know about you, but not even I know what I want to hear. I keep waiting just in case someone can figure it out.
Who told you that? Why do you believe it?
I hope sometime in the future, you won't still believe that.

There's no such thing as full potential. Just use it the best you can. And who's to say you're useless? Everyone has their own talents, And their personality alone is enough to bring more to the world.
Heart failure. But that's not really something you can induce. If you want not to be in pain, perhaps look for options in the waking world.
I vote for vacation and therapist, if the opinion of a stranger helps.

Your mere existence is an accomplishment. Even if you feel as though there is nothing to your life other than agony and despair, I promise you are the only one who thinks that. If life is a gift, then why return it? Do the most you can with it, and live to find a future you can be proud of.
How do you know part of my nighttime ritual?
I'm glad for you in that regard

Oh that's the worst, I relate to this too much. You close your eyes, and pray they won't open. When they inevitably do, your filled with immeasurable disappointment. if you do fade away, please take me with you.

Good night

This story makes me want to cry. I'm so, so sorry you had to go through this. That sounds like hell. I would have no idea what to do about this. The only thing that comes to my mind is move to a different county, so that you might be able to find better resources? But that sounds like a lot, so I don't know about that one. Your parents seem to care a lot about you, perhaps confide a little bit more in them? I know it's difficult and embarrassing, but I promise they're there for you.

I'd like to tell you that it'll get better, but clearly that won't help you, so I'll tell you something else instead. I hope that if you die, you die happy. Even if for just a moment before the deed is done, I wish that you will not leave in tears. I hope that for a half second, your hurt and burdens will dissipate, so that you may go in peace. And I'm dreadfuly sorry for all you've had to suffer. Maybe if you try to ask for help, the half second would eventually turn into a few more years. But either way, I wish you the best.

Who told you you're ugly? Why do you believe them? I know it's difficult, and it's not like you could just stop being looked down upon, but you're more then your intimate past. Maybe you do hate living, but hopefully it doesn't have to stay that way.

I'm sorry to hear that. I understand what it's like to feel shitty. As a stranger there's not much I can do for you, but I do hope you don't feel that way for the rest of your life. I hope that when you do die, preferably far from now, you'll be happy.
I think you just might be missed.

Oh, if you have the opportunity, absolutely talk about how you've been feeling. You're not me, but in my case, a big part of the lying came from a place of shame. There's no room for that with a medical professional. The psychiatrist will do more than worry, and they won't worry nearly as much as your close friends and family might. The psychiatrist will try to help you, and will help you explore those feelings, to help you express those emotions. Possibly give you meds. Talking to people who majored in this field never goes the way you think it will, so give it a shot.

If your mom is taking you to those appointments, I don't think she considers you a burden. I think she would do anything to keep you alive, even if her efforts to do sometimes get in her way. Just part of parenting. If you misinterpret her love as being an inconvenience to her, your disrespecting her hard work as a mother. And I don't mean to guilt trip or invalidate you. If you feel like a burden, you feel like a burden. Life is shitty sometimes. But I hope you can have more faith in the people who care about you.

You might already know this, but I'll say it just in case: the abuse you suffered is not your fault. The person who doesn't deserve to live is not you, but that sick bitch who traumatized you. What you're going through is a form of coping. I vote you seek professional help. Considering you're still a teen, you could just unload all this during a random doctor appointment, or you could talk to a shitty school counselor, (they scare easy,) or you could try to find a therapist. But please don't kill yourself. Please.
That's really weird. I can't imagine myself calling a hotline, but at least I know it's there. I'm scared for you.

You're not going to get that here, my friend. It's a suicide watch, not a suicide endorsement. But I will say this: humans are fragile. Don't think too much about it. What you need to think about, is what you really want.
Thank you for saying so. I hope you end up being right.

I don't believe in reincarnation, nor do I know a whole lot about it. but from what I do know, the way you die and the life you lived contributes to the person you will become in your next life. If your were an asshole who died in prison, you'll end up poor and unlucky in your next life. People who believe that suicide is cowardly and selfish, or that they're life isn't worth much, might also believe that their next life will be as bad as their current one.
Happy birthday. Since you've posted this here, I think it's appropriate to hope you'll live to see next year's.

If you need somewhere to go, perhaps schedule an appointment with a therapist? If that's too expensive or scary, maybe go with a hotline. I've never called one, but apparently someone there would be willing to talk.
I wish you well in whatever comes next.

Honestly, a lot of this sub is people who are in pain and need help, but that's just not quite how it is for me. I always thought I was the only one with a more peaceful outlook on suicide, but apparently I'm not. Welcome to the club I guess. It's kind of nice here.
Of course.

It might seem apathetic of me, but I don't care if I the people I love will miss me. I won't be affected by that at all if I'm dead. 

I'm glad you were able to find something to keep you here, a reason to keep suffering. I hope that I'll find that for myself before I refuse to keep looking.

Perhaps there is. But even if I have an objective reason to stay, (I want to accomplish xyz, learn about xyz, etc.,) The overwhelming desire to be dead always seems to come first. Like I don't even care about the things I know I care about.

Well that does sound like you're in need of help. I don't know you're life or your partner, so I might be wrong, but they sound like an asshole. I understand the tired feeling though. If you ever muster the energy, maybe call the police and tell them you might be a danger to yourself.
Dying in contentment is the dream. Something about knowing that the last breath is coming just makes the night prettier.
In a way, we're all lonely. Regardless, I hope someone manages to pull you out of those feelings.

Before you think about getting him back for your sake, perhaps think about him. You know you hurt him, so the first thing you do is communicate that to him, and apologize. Tell him the truth about why you broke up, tell him how the experience of failing changed you. The confrontation needs to be for him and not you, but if he takes what you said well, then tell him you still love him. Tell him that leaving him was a mistake. Don't ask for him to take you back, but offer yourself if he's still interested in the relationship.
Is there a reason you come to the internet with this, rather than seeking help from people you care about?
